last_assistant_message:
Research complete. My main report was delivered via SubagentHandback, and the late-arriving supplement (Walmart, U.S. Army, Providence, Barts Health NHS, FedEx) was sent to the main conversation via SendMessage since the handback channel delivers only once.

**Summary of what was delivered:**

- **Bucket 1 — Adoption (8 stats):** SHRM "State of AI in HR 2026" (39% of orgs use AI in HR; recruiting 27%, L&D 17%; n=1,908); SHRM 2025 (43% of HR pros, up from 26%); SHRM 2024 task breakdown (64% recruiting, only 7% AI video screening); LinkedIn Future of Recruiting (37% of recruiting orgs, ~20% of work week saved); Gartner (88% of HR leaders see no significant business value); WEF Future of Jobs 2025; SHRM worker data; plus a vendor-sponsored "80% adopt / 10% see gains" reality check.

- **Bucket 2 — Deployed (10+ named, quantified):** IBM AskHR (94% of routine inquiries, −40% HR budget), Microsoft Employee Self-Service Agent, Chipotle/Paradox (75% faster hiring), McDonald's, Fontainebleau Las Vegas (6,500 hires/4 months), Walmart, 7-Eleven, JLL, Standard Chartered/Gloat (~$49k saved per redeploy), Schneider Electric, TCS, U.S. Army, Providence, Barts Health NHS, plus backups. Spans tech, retail, restaurant, hospitality, government, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, and UK public sector.

- **Bucket 3 — Emerging + governance:** agentic HR (Workday Autopilot/MCP, SAP Joule, Salesforce Agentforce, Amazon Connect Talent, HireVue AI Interviewer, Apriare); the full regulatory picture — EEOC guidance removed but not rescinded + 2026 NEP abandoning disparate impact; NYC LL144 (no fines ever issued, Dec 2025 Comptroller audit found enforcement gaps); Illinois HB 3773 (live Jan 1, 2026); **EU AI Act high-risk obligations delayed to Dec 2, 2027 by the AI Omnibus (Reg. 2026/1744)**; **Colorado AI Act repealed and replaced (SB 26-189)**; California ADS regs; and AI-hiring litigation (Amazon, iTutorGroup, Mobley v. Workday, Eightfold FCRA, Stanford bias study).

- **A "do NOT use" list** of 12 unverifiable/misattributed/outdated stats, including several premises the research proved wrong (the EU Aug 2026 date, Colorado's June 2026 delay, "LL144 fines," the Maryland law, and the misattributed "43% of recruiters").

**Method caveat carried through the report:** WebSearch was unauthorized this session and mainstream engines were bot-blocked, so every item was verified by direct fetches (WebFetch and the r.jina.ai reader proxy) plus Google News RSS with a working URL decoder. Company/vendor self-reported figures are labeled as such.
